## Confirmed findings

### nmap

#### f-nmap-22-scan1: Open TCP port 22 (ssh)

In-scope asset: scanme.nmap.org
Source tool: nmap
Source action: scan_nmap_1
Severity: info
Severity rationale: Open port exposure alone is not an exploitable vulnerability.
Confidence: confirmed
Description: The SSH service port is open and accessible from the network.
CWE: CWE-200
Reproducibility: POSIX shell: nmap -sT -p 22 scanme.nmap.org
Remediation: Restrict SSH access to authorized management networks using network ACLs or host-based firewall rules.

Evidence (raw excerpt):

```
22/tcp open  ssh     OpenSSH 6.6.1p1 Ubuntu 2ubuntu2.13 (Ubuntu Linux; protocol 2.0)
```

### nuclei

#### f-nuclei-headers-scan2: Missing HTTP Security Headers (http-missing-security-headers)

In-scope asset: scanme.nmap.org
Source tool: nuclei
Source action: scan_nuclei_2
Severity: medium
Severity rationale: Absence of defensive HTTP response headers increases client vulnerability to clickjacking, MIME-sniffing, and cross-site content injection.
Confidence: confirmed
Description: The server response lacks recommended defensive headers including Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, and X-Frame-Options.
CWE: CWE-693
Reproducibility: POSIX shell: nuclei -u http://scanme.nmap.org -id http-missing-security-headers
Remediation: Configure web server to return Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, and Strict-Transport-Security headers.

Evidence (raw excerpt):

````json
{
  "extracted-results": [
    "Content-Security-Policy",
    "Strict-Transport-Security",
    "X-Frame-Options"
  ],
  "info": {
    "name": "Missing HTTP Security Headers",
    "severity": "medium"
  },
  "matched-at": "http://scanme.nmap.org",
  "template-id": "http-missing-security-headers"
}
````
